jobs.title: Transformation Risk and Advisory Director
jobs.description:
As a Director in PMO / Project Management Managed Services Team, you will bring deep expertise in transformation delivery across IT, compliance and people change programs. You will be responsible for setting up and leading transformation teams, including the PMO practices, Project Management teams, driving thought leadership and sales activities within a consultancy environment Our PMO & Project Management Managed Services Team, focuses on assisting clients that are going through large transformations ($100 Mil - $5 bil) by providing services that cover transformation strategy, transformation risk management, transformation program management or other related services. The core focus of this team is to work with clients that are going through large transformation programs and help them make these programs successful. We bring an integrated people, process and technology approach to these projects and can support the client from “strategy to execution” with their transformation program.

Meaningful work you’ll be part of

As a PMO & Project Management Managed Services Director, you'll work as part of a team of problem solvers, helping to solve complex business issues from strategy to execution. Responsibilities include but are not limited to: 

Oversee end-to-end delivery, including project economics, across multiple consulting projects and teams. Lead the engagement team to deliver high-quality results on schedule, within budget, and meeting client and internal standards
PMO set up and delivery experience including reporting on progress to c-suite sponsors 
Manage an engagement team to the production of quality deliverables on time and on budget and in line with client expectations and internal standards 
Lead pursuit teams and proposal development including innovative approaches and methodologies tailored to address specific client transformation requirements 
Build new relationships and leverage existing relationships within the industry to identify large transformation programs where PwC can take a Transformation Risk & Advisory role
Building strong networks within the firm to spot help ensure our clients see the best of PwC 
Identify gaps in the market and spot opportunities to create value propositions
Help clients develop business cases and justifications for transformational projects 
Stay abreast of key industry developments both within Canada and globally 
Understand the operational implications of client’s strategies
Grow and develop our team through hands on training and coaching 
Define and develop new consultant assets and accelerators to support our services  
Promote and encourage others to value difference when working in diverse teams
Communicate complex material effectively in written and oral formats to various audiences 

Experiences And Skills You’ll Use To Solve  

Proven experience in leading PMO / PM practices for large transformation programs / portfolio’s ($100M+ budgets)
Hands-on experience justifying, managing or delivering large business, compliance and IT transformations. Credibility with clients by demonstrating subject matter expertise and knowledge for Transformation delivery and associated key risks
Ability to develop and manage strategic client relationships while providing the highest quality client work across multiple client projects 
Track record of leading sales activities, including business development, proposal creation, and closing new consulting engagements
Managing and delivering significant business results that reflects strategic and creative thinking, individual initiative and motivating teams 
Extensive management consulting experience, with knowledge of strategy, operations, technology and AI to drive efficiencies
Demonstrated thought leadership in transformation delivery, including published insights, speaking engagements, or recognized expertise
An interest in upskilling for a digital world, technology trends and impacts of AI, an openness to learning new tools and improving operating models
Excellent leadership, organizational and verbal and written communication skills. Proven leader with extensive abilities to build solid and collaborative relationships with team members, foster a productive teamwork environment, and leverage diverse views
A demonstrated commitment to valuing differences, developing and coaching diverse teams, and ensuring diverse perspectives are heard 
An MBA or CA and Program Management certification or equivalent is considered an asset
PwC Canada is committed to cultivating an inclusive, hybrid work environment. Exact expectations for your team can be discussed with your interviewer 

This newly created role reflects our commitment to growth and delivering distinctive value for our clients and stakeholders.

jobs.description:
Come make your difference in communities across Canada, where authenticity, trust and making connections is valued – as we shape the future of Canadian retail, together. Our unique position as one of the country's largest employers, coupled with our commitment to positively impact the lives of all Canadians, provides our colleagues a range of opportunities and experiences to help Canadians Live Life Well®.

At Loblaw Companies Limited, we succeed through collaboration and commitment and set a high bar for ourselves and those around us. Whether you are just starting your career, re-entering the workforce, or looking for a new job, this is where you belong.

Loblaw Technology and Analytics power some of Canada’s most game-changing retail solutions. We connect Canadians to things that matter most. Food, health, beauty, money, and time. Curiosity drives us as we solve complex problems at pace and lay foundation for a secure organization today while influencing a better future for our customers tomorrow. Join us and work alongside some of Canada’s most diverse and talented innovators supporting retail, digital customer solutions and analytical platforms.

The Impact You’ll Make

Transforming how Loblaw prevents fraud, reduces shrink and operational loss through intelligence, technology, and analytics. This is a significant enterprise leadership opportunity to modernize how Loblaw identifies, prevents, and reduces fraud, shrink and operational loss across retail, pharmacy, digital and supply chain operations. The mandate combines commercial judgment, intelligence-led prevention, security operations, data and technology modernization, and enterprise-wide change.

The successful executive will inherit an established asset protection and security organization and help evolve its operating model. The opportunity includes connecting information across functions, improving the use of analytics and intelligence, reducing manual effort, strengthening preventive controls, and translating insights into measurable financial and operational outcomes. The role reports to the Chief Technology & Analytics Officer and works closely with field operations leaders and stakeholders across the business.

What You’ll Do

Own the enterprise fraud, shrink and loss reduction roadmap, identifying root causes and prioritizing measurable opportunities.
Modernize operating models, workflows and cross-functional accountability across Asset Protection, fraud, investigations, and operations.
Advance intelligence-led prevention by integrating signals from stores, digital channels, inventory, investigations, and emerging threats.
Guide the evolution of centralized security and intelligence operations, including the GSOC (Global Security Operations Center), and improve how data becomes coordinated action.
Champion analytics, automation and technologies such as case management, video intelligence, exception analytics, and retail crime intelligence tools, with disciplined investment ROI.
Strengthen responses to organized retail crime and major fraud, and support partnerships with law enforcement, government, and industry.
Partner with field operations, Supply Chain, Pharmacy, Digital, Finance, Technology, HR and Legal to implement practical solutions and protect customer and colleague experiences.
Lead and develop an experienced organization, building leadership depth, accountability, and a culture of continuous improvement.

What You’ll Bring

Senior executive leadership with demonstrated enterprise transformation and operating-model modernization.
Substantial experience in fraud prevention, intelligence, investigations, operational loss, or adjacent relevant risk disciplines.
A track record of measurable outcomes in loss reduction, improved controls, operational effectiveness, or financial value creation.
Experience using data, analytics, and technology to connect fragmented information and enable more proactive decision-making.
Strong relationships with field or distributed operations leadership, with the ability to influence change without direct authority.
Commercial and financial judgment, including investment prioritization and return-on-investment evaluation.
Experience leading senior leaders and working across complex, matrixed organizations.
Substantial experience in fraud prevention, intelligence, investigations, asset protection, or operational loss reduction, with demonstrated responsibility for preventing financial or inventory losses in complex operating environments.
CPP/CFE and English/French bilingualism are assets.

Advise executives and the Board on financial performance, regulatory capital, liquidity, control health, and emerging risks.
Partner across Tax, Treasury, Legal, Compliance, Operations, Product, and Technology to align reporting, capital, liquidity, and strategy.
Build organizational capability through talent development, succession planning, outsourced-provider governance, and KPI/SLA accountability.
Drive responsible automation and AI adoption that improves reporting quality, efficiency, control effectiveness, and auditability.

Successfully passed the Chief Financial Officer Qualifying Examination and the Partners, Directors and Officers Qualifying Examination, each administered by the Canadian Securities Institute (CSI) and the Canadian Investment Regulatory Organization (CIRO).
5+ years of direct ownership and preparation of both CIRO Form 1 and Form 31-103F1 for a Canadian regulated entity.
Direct experience managing the filing lifecycle, including calculations, accounting judgments, review and sign-off, submission, regulator follow-up, and remediation.
Experience in a self-clearing or introducing broker-dealer environment, with expertise in dealer capital adequacy, regulatory capital, liquidity, and related controls.
CPA or equivalent accounting designation required.
Expert knowledge of IFRS, NI 31-103, Form 31-103F1, CIRO capital adequacy, and Canadian securities-regulatory reporting.
Demonstrated enterprise-level leadership, regulator-facing judgment, executive communication, and Board influence.
Utilizes generative AI responsibly, maintaining human oversight to deliver business-ready outputs and drive measurable improvements in workflow efficiency, cost, and quality.

jobs.title: Director of Digital Operations
jobs.description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, which manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Director of Digital Operations based in Canada.

We are seeking an experienced and strategic Director of Digital Operations to lead and optimize the delivery of comprehensive digital marketing services across a large portfolio of small and medium-sized businesses. In this senior leadership role, you will oversee SEO, paid advertising, social media marketing, and website content operations while driving service quality, customer satisfaction, and business performance. You will lead multidisciplinary teams, establish scalable processes, and ensure marketing initiatives deliver measurable results and long-term customer value. A key focus will be accelerating digital transformation through artificial intelligence, automation, and emerging search technologies, including AEO and GEO. Working closely with Product, Technology, Sales, and Customer Success teams, you will shape innovative service offerings and improve operational efficiency. This is an opportunity to influence business growth, strengthen customer retention, and build a high-performing digital marketing organization in a fully remote environment.

Accountabilities

Lead and oversee the end-to-end delivery of digital marketing services, including Search Engine Optimization (SEO), Pay-Per-Click advertising (PPC), Social Media Marketing (SMM), and website content management, ensuring consistent quality and measurable customer outcomes.
Design and implement scalable operational processes, workflows, and service delivery standards to efficiently manage a large portfolio of customer campaigns.
Establish, monitor, and optimize key performance indicators (KPIs) covering campaign effectiveness, service quality, turnaround times, team productivity, customer retention, and profitability.
Develop and execute annual operating plans for digital services, aligning operational priorities with broader business objectives and growth strategies.
Drive improvements in search visibility, website traffic, lead generation, conversion rates, and overall marketing return on investment (ROI).
Oversee campaign performance analysis using Google Analytics 4 (GA4), Google Search Console, Google Ads, and other marketing analytics platforms.
Establish consistent reporting frameworks, performance benchmarks, and actionable recommendations to continuously improve customer results.
Monitor digital marketing trends, search engine algorithm changes, competitive developments, and emerging technologies to maintain service relevance and competitiveness.
Collaborate with Product Management to enhance existing digital marketing solutions and introduce new services that address evolving customer needs.
Lead the adoption of AI-powered tools, automation, and intelligent workflows to improve marketing effectiveness, content production, team productivity, and operational efficiency.
Drive the evolution of traditional SEO practices toward AI Search Optimization, including Answer Engine Optimization (AEO) and Generative Engine Optimization (GEO), improving customer visibility across traditional and AI-powered search platforms.
Partner with Product and Technology teams to integrate emerging AI capabilities into everyday marketing operations and service delivery.
Champion a customer-first culture by ensuring campaigns deliver meaningful business outcomes and contribute to long-term satisfaction and retention.
Identify underperforming campaigns and customers at risk of leaving, developing and implementing corrective action plans to address issues proactively.
Work closely with Account Management, Customer Success, and Sales teams to strengthen the customer experience, resolve escalations, and improve retention.
Provide strategic guidance and leadership when addressing complex customer concerns, campaign performance challenges, and service delivery issues.
Lead, coach, and develop digital marketing managers and individual contributors, establishing clear performance expectations, accountability frameworks, and professional development plans.
Build a high-performance culture focused on collaboration, innovation, operational excellence, customer outcomes, and continuous improvement.
Assess staffing needs, resource allocation, and organizational capabilities to support business expansion and evolving service requirements.
Manage the financial and operational performance of digital services, including budgets, staffing, gross margins, and cost of service delivery.
Improve productivity, resource utilization, and revenue per employee while maintaining high service quality and customer satisfaction.
Partner with Sales and Finance teams to forecast demand, staffing requirements, and operational capacity.
Identify opportunities to improve profitability and operational efficiency while preserving or enhancing customer results.
Provide regular performance updates to senior leadership covering operational KPIs, financial results, customer outcomes, and strategic improvement initiatives.

Requirements

Required Qualifications and Experience:

Bachelor's degree in Marketing, Business, Communications, or a related discipline, or equivalent relevant professional experience.
At least 7 years of experience in digital marketing, including substantial responsibility for managing customer-facing digital marketing service delivery.
Demonstrated experience leading digital marketing teams, including managers and individual contributors.
Strong expertise in SEO, paid search advertising, social media marketing, website content optimization, and digital marketing performance measurement.
Previous experience managing digital marketing services for external customer portfolios within an agency, SaaS-enabled services organization, or similar business environment.
Proven ability to manage operational performance, develop scalable processes, improve service quality, and optimize team productivity.
Strong working knowledge of Google Analytics 4 (GA4), Google Search Console, Google Ads, and digital marketing analytics and reporting tools.
Experience implementing AI-powered tools, automation, or AI-assisted workflows to enhance marketing performance and operational efficiency.
Strong financial management, analytical, organizational, and strategic leadership capabilities.
Excellent communication, decision-making, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to translate business objectives into actionable operational strategies.
Demonstrated ability to collaborate effectively with Sales, Product Management, Customer Success, Finance, Technology teams, and senior leadership.

Preferred Qualifications And Experience

Experience managing digital marketing operations at scale across hundreds or thousands of small and medium-sized business customers.
Background in professional services industries, such as dental, veterinary, accounting, legal, healthcare, or related sectors.
Experience with AI Search Optimization, including Answer Engine Optimization (AEO), Generative Engine Optimization (GEO), generative search visibility, and emerging search technologies.
Familiarity with AI-driven marketing automation, predictive analytics, and marketing intelligence solutions.
Experience leading organizational transformation, operational restructuring, or large-scale process improvement initiatives.
Familiarity with marketing technology and analytics platforms such as SEMrush, Ahrefs, CallRail, Looker Studio, and comparable solutions.
Strong ability to anticipate industry changes, identify innovation opportunities, and translate emerging technologies into practical business improvements.
Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a fully remote, fast-paced, results-oriented environment.
Availability for occasional overtime or weekend work when business needs require it.
Willingness to travel occasionally, depending on operational and management requirements.
Ability to meet the physical requirements of the position, including prolonged periods of sedentary work and occasional lifting of up to 20 pounds.

Benefits

Competitive annual salary ranging from $140,000 to $160,000, depending on experience and qualifications.
Fully remote working arrangement.
Full-time employment opportunity in a strategic senior leadership position.
Opportunity to lead a large-scale digital marketing organization and influence business-wide operational strategy.
Exposure to innovative technologies, including artificial intelligence, marketing automation, and next-generation search optimization.
Opportunity to shape and develop new digital marketing services and operational capabilities.
Collaborative working environment involving cross-functional teams and senior leadership.
Significant scope for professional growth, strategic influence, and organizational impact.

jobs.description:
Reports to: Chief Executive Officer | Location: Toronto, Ontario [hybrid] | Full-time, permanent

About Us

Appficiency is a global technology and professional services firm that solves complex business challenges through the intelligent application of enterprise software, automation, and AI. We're a proud Oracle NetSuite Alliance Partner; Salesforce Crest Partner; Microsoft Gold Certified Partner, and much more: our evolution has taken us well beyond a single platform, making us a multi-technology advisory and implementation partner across ERP, CRM, cloud platforms, and AI-driven solutions. What sets us apart is a "technical-first" approach, teams who understand both business logic and deep system architecture paired with a genuine belief that our people are our greatest strength, and that's who we invest in first.

The Opportunity

As our first CFO, you will be the senior-most financial leader of the organization — owning financial strategy, acquisition strategy and the overall fiscal health of the business as we navigate our next phase of growth as a services-led technology firm, scaling through both organic growth and acquisitions. You'll work closely with the CEO and the executive team to drive sustainable revenue growth and profitability, improve financial performance and build a finance function that gives leadership timely, reliable information for decisions. Our day-to-day finance operations are sound; this role adds the senior leadership layer above them. It suits a seasoned finance executive who can do three things well: build the function (processes, reporting and budgeting), develop the team and lead acquisitions from screening through integration.

What You'll Do

Develop and execute financial strategies that align with the company's growth objectives, including a growth plan that separates organic growth from acquisition-driven growth and tracks both against actual results
Oversee all financial operations, including FP&A, accounting, treasury, budgeting, and risk management across our Toronto and Philippines teams
Lead the strategic financial planning process, including long-term projections and capital allocation decisions made with the CEO
Act as the CEO's senior deputy on financial and operational matters, able to represent the company and lead decisions in the CEO's absence
Build and deliver a monthly management reporting package (results, budget-to-actual analysis, key performance indicators and commentary) on a fixed calendar, so leadership receives the information it needs without having to request it
Lead the annual budget with department heads so each leader understands and owns their budget, and connect it to the unit economics of the business
Oversee company cash flow, investments, and capital structure optimization
Manage financial reporting and ensure compliance with regulatory requirements, including tax, payroll and statutory filings in each country where we operate
Set revenue recognition, billing and project accounting policies for fixed-fee, time-and-materials and software resale contracts
Lead mergers and acquisitions from end to end: set acquisition criteria; screen opportunities sourced by our advisors; lead valuation, financial due diligence and deal structuring; and plan post-acquisition integration
Manage relationships with banks, lenders, auditors and external advisors; lead any future financing
Build and lead the finance and accounting team; coach and develop current team members into larger roles and add capability (such as FP&A) as the business grows
Analyze key professional services metrics (utilization, realization, project margin, backlog, collections) and software metrics (recurring revenue, renewals, churn) to drive profitability and growth decisions
Partner with the CEO and executive team on strategic decision-making and operational efficiency
Collaborate with the CTO and other executives to align financial and technology strategy
Partner with the leader of our internal transformation program so finance processes and reporting support company-wide operating improvements
Identify financial risks, maintain effective internal controls and develop mitigation strategies to protect company assets
Prepare the business for potential future milestones (e.g. significant acquisitions, major growth investments or a future transaction)

What You'll Bring

Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, or related field; Master's degree or MBA preferred
12-15+ years of progressive finance experience, including significant time as a CFO or senior finance executive in a professional services or technology firm, ideally an IT consulting or systems integration business
CPA designation (or equivalent international accounting designation) required; CFA an asset
Executive experience with professional services and software business models and associated revenue recognition
Proven experience scaling a mid-market business toward $100M in revenue, including growth through acquisitions
A builder's track record: designing finance processes, management reporting and budgeting from the ground up, ideally as a company's first CFO
Strong track record driving financial strategy in high-growth, founder-led or owner-managed environments
Deep understanding of professional services economics (utilization, rates, project margin) and software metrics and their strategic implications
Excellent leadership skills, with experience building and scaling finance teams and mentoring early-career finance leaders
Outstanding communication skills, comfortable engaging the CEO, department heads, lenders and acquisition counterparties; able to explain financial results clearly to non-financial leaders
International finance experience (multi-country teams and foreign currency) is a plus
Hands-on experience with Oracle NetSuite (or a comparable cloud ERP) is a strong asset

What Will Set You Apart

A track record of successfully leading acquisitions of professional services or technology businesses, from screening through integration
Deep fluency in services and software unit economics and how they inform strategic decision-making
A reputation for clear, credible financial communication with owners, lenders and leadership teams
Experience preparing a company for significant milestones (acquisition, major scale-up)
A collaborative, tech-forward mindset — comfortable partnering with product and technology leaders
Experience coaching a high-potential finance manager into a senior leadership role
Comfort stepping into a finance framework established by an interim CFO or external advisors and making it your own

What Success Looks Like

The company's financial strategy directly enables and accelerates growth objectives
The CEO and leadership team view you as a trusted, credible voice on financial health and strategy
Leadership receives a monthly management reporting package on a fixed calendar, without having to request it
Department heads own their budgets and use them to run their areas
Acquisition opportunities are screened against clear criteria and the transactions you lead are executed and integrated smoothly
The finance team operates as a strategic partner to the business, not just a reporting function
The Finance team has grown into larger roles, with clear accountabilities and succession in place
Financial risk is proactively managed, and the company is well-positioned for its next growth milestone

jobs.description:
Executive Vice President of Project Management

Detailed Job Description

Job Overview

The Executive Vice President (EVP) of Project Management is responsible for providing comprehensive leadership and oversight of the company’s project management framework, project portfolio, and the execution of major projects. The EVP defines enterprise-level project management strategy, ensuring that all projects are implemented successfully in alignment with established strategic goals, budgetary plans, timelines, and quality standards. This role holds full accountability for project planning, execution, resource allocation, budget control, risk management, team leadership, and performance monitoring, with the objective of driving the standardization, formalization, and efficiency of the company’s project management system.

The EVP of Project Management is tasked with translating the company’s strategic objectives into actionable project plans, overseeing cross-departmental and cross-business-unit collaboration, and ensuring that major initiatives are delivered on time, within budget, and to the required quality standards. Working closely with the CEO, COO, CFO, heads of business units, and senior project management teams, the EVP provides strategic project management support for major investments, business transformation initiatives, and long-term development strategies, while continuously enhancing the organization’s overall project delivery capabilities.

Key Responsibilities

I. Project Management Strategy and Executive Leadership

Develop and implement an enterprise-wide project management strategy, ensuring that project management objectives are aligned with the company’s corporate strategy, operational plans, and long-term business goals. Provide comprehensive leadership to the project management department and relevant management teams, establishing unified standards, workflows, and execution mechanisms. Determine the direction, management priorities, and resource allocation plans for key projects based on the company’s business development needs. Monitor the execution of the project management strategy and provide regular reports to the CEO and senior leadership team regarding overall project progress, critical issues, and the outcomes of strategic implementation.

II. Project Portfolio Management and Prioritization

Assume full responsibility for the management and oversight of the company’s project portfolio. Evaluate the strategic value, commercial viability, resource requirements, and expected returns of individual projects to ensure that investments remain aligned with the company’s overall business objectives. Establish mechanisms for project initiation, approval, prioritization, and periodic review, while optimizing the allocation of resources and the sequence of execution across various projects. Oversee interdependencies, resource conflicts, and schedule coordination among multiple projects, adjusting the portfolio management plan as necessary. Collaborate with finance and business units to ensure that key projects receive the appropriate funding, personnel, and technical support. III. Project Planning and Execution Oversight

Lead the overall planning and execution management of major projects, ensuring that project scope, objectives, timelines, budgets, deliverables, and the division of responsibilities are clearly defined. Oversee project managers and their teams to ensure work progresses according to approved project plans, while conducting regular reviews of project milestones, task completion, and the quality of deliverables. For complex, cross-departmental, or high-priority projects, participate directly in key decision-making and execution oversight, addressing major issues that arise during implementation in a timely manner. Ensure that every phase of the project—from initiation, planning, and execution to monitoring and final delivery—complies with the company’s management requirements.

IV. Budget Management and Resource Allocation

Manage budget planning, cost oversight, and resource allocation at the project management level, collaborating with the Chief Financial Officer (CFO) and the finance department to establish project budgets, funding requirements, and cost-control plans. Monitor variances between actual expenditures and approved budgets, analyze the causes of any cost overruns, and develop appropriate corrective measures. Coordinate human resources, technical equipment, external vendors, and other necessary resources to ensure project teams possess the capabilities and conditions required to complete their tasks. Promote resource sharing and cross-project optimization to enhance resource utilization, reduce execution costs, and ensure that project investments yield the expected business value.

V. Project Performance and Schedule Management

Establish a unified corporate project performance management system and define key performance indicators (KPIs)—such as project completion rates, milestone achievement rates, budget and schedule variances, delivery quality, and project returns. Organize regular project review meetings to assess execution progress, cost status, and actual outcomes. Ensure that project managers submit timely progress reports, risk assessments, and performance analyses, enabling management to maintain an accurate understanding of project status. For projects experiencing delays, budget overruns, or quality issues, coordinate with relevant teams to develop recovery plans and improvement strategies, ensuring that projects are brought back on track.

VI. Cross-Departmental Coordination and Stakeholder Management

Foster effective collaboration between project management teams and various business functions—including operations, finance, engineering, technology, procurement, sales, marketing, and human resources—to ensure alignment on project objectives, resource allocation, and delivery requirements. Resolve conflicts regarding responsibilities, communication barriers, resource contention, or execution challenges that may arise in cross-departmental projects. Responsible for high-level communication with clients, suppliers, partners, and other key stakeholders to ensure that project requirements are accurately understood and critical matters are addressed in a timely manner. In the event of major project disputes or issues impacting overall delivery, organize relevant management personnel to develop and implement solutions.

VII. Project Risk, Quality, and Compliance Management

Establish an enterprise-level project risk management framework, overseeing project teams as they identify, assess, and manage potential risks related to schedules, budgets, technology, contracts, supply chains, and operations. Develop mechanisms for project risk reporting, issue escalation, and contingency response to ensure that significant risks are escalated promptly and resolved effectively. Collaborate with legal, compliance, quality management, and internal audit departments to ensure project execution adheres to applicable laws, regulations, contractual requirements, industry standards, and internal company policies. Supervise project quality control and delivery acceptance processes, drive the implementation of corrective and preventive actions, and mitigate the risks of project failure or operational losses.

VIII. Project Management System Optimization and Team Development

Continuously refine the company’s project management policies, standardized processes, and management tools, while advancing the development and operational capabilities of the Project Management Office (PMO). Introduce appropriate project management methodologies, digital management platforms, and data analytics technologies to enhance efficiency in project planning, schedule tracking, resource management, and performance reporting. Lead the development of project management talent, establishing performance evaluation, professional training, and succession planning mechanisms for project managers. Consolidate experience and best practices from major projects to foster knowledge sharing and continuous process improvement, thereby elevating the company’s professional standards in project management and its overall delivery capacity.

Typically requires 18+ years of experience in project management, project execution, engineering management, or corporate operations.

At least 8 years of senior management experience, with a proven track record of leading large-scale project management departments, Project Management Offices (PMOs), or multiple project teams.

Extensive experience in managing large project portfolios, complex cross-departmental projects, and enterprise-level strategic initiatives.

Drive quarterly and annual cloud savings targets using transparent methodologies for hard savings, unit-cost improvements, and cost avoidance.
Identify cloud cost drivers and translate findings into practical, measurable optimization initiatives.

Strong stakeholder management and influencing skills across business and technical partners.

The role also provides leadership and direction for the Human Resources function, supporting the development of a high-performing and engaged workforce. Working closely with internal teams, airline partners, vendors, and stakeholders, the successful candidate will help shape the airport’s long-term strategy and contribute to the continued growth and success of one of Atlantic Canada’s most important transportation hubs.

Achievement of Financial Goals

As a member of the senior leadership team, partners with the CEO to translate the airport's strategic vision into long-term plans, annual business objectives, and measurable financial outcomes; leads initiatives that support sustainable growth and long-term financial viability.
Leads the annual business planning, budgeting, and forecasting processes, working collaboratively with all departments to develop financial plans that support organizational priorities.
Provides strategic financial analysis, insights, and recommendations to support operational, commercial, and capital investment decisions across the organization.
Leads the financial evaluation, negotiation, and ongoing performance monitoring of commercial agreements with airlines, concessionaires, tenants, and vendors.

Management & Performance Reporting

Leads all external financial audits and serves as the primary liaison with auditors, financial institutions, and lending partners.
Manages the organization's insurance portfolio and enterprise risk management program, identifying and mitigating risks to support operational and financial objectives.
Serves as the organization's subject matter expert on airport fees and charges, Airport Improvement Fees (AIF), lease structures, and commercial pricing.
Ensures compliance with the Federal Ground Lease and related reporting, procurement, insurance, and public accountability requirements.

Leadership & Team Development

Leads the Finance & Administration team in a collaborative, high-performance environment, setting clear expectations and supporting employee growth, development, and succession planning.
Provides strategic leadership and oversight for the Human Resources function through the HR Manager, including workforce planning, employee relations, labour relations, and organizational effectiveness.
Oversees the Corporate Board Secretary function, ensuring effective governance processes, accurate board records, and administrative support for the Board of Directors.

Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Business Administration, Commerce, or a related field.
Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA) designation required.
Additional education or professional development in leadership, governance, risk management, or human resources would be considered an asset.

Experience serving as a key member of a senior leadership team, contributing to organizational strategy, business planning, and decision-making.
Demonstrated success leading financial planning, budgeting, forecasting, reporting, audits, treasury management, and risk management functions.
Experience presenting financial results, strategic recommendations, and business cases to Boards of Directors, Audit Committees, or similar governance bodies.
Experience evaluating, negotiating, and managing commercial agreements and business relationships with customers, vendors, tenants and airlines.
Experience providing leadership and oversight to human resources functions, including workforce planning and organizational development; direct HR leadership experience and labour relations is considered an asset.

Ability to lead organizational change and influence stakeholders at all levels, including executives, Board members, business partners, and external stakeholders.

We are looking for a Director, Portfolio Management & Governance within the Technology Project Management Office.

The Director, Portfolio Management & Governance reports to the AVP, Program Management & Governance and is accountable for the integrated planning, governance, and delivery oversight of technology investments within the Canada Operations & Business Enablement portfolio. The Director works closely with senior business and technology leaders to establish priorities, evaluate investment trade-offs, manage portfolio-level risks and dependencies, and ensure initiatives deliver measurable business value within approved financial and capacity constraints. The role leads a team of Program Managers and Project Managers and serves as a trusted advisor and escalation point for portfolio delivery.

The Director, Portfolio Management & Governance is outcome-focused and capable of leading high-profile, highly complex, or ground-breaking programs of work while providing clear, credible advice to senior leadership.

What you will do:

Planning:

Lead the development of the annual portfolio delivery plan and budget within Technology, and work with business partners to refresh a multi‑year delivery roadmap that aligns with strategic priorities.
Collaborate with Technology and Business Portfolio Leaders to assess and socialize priorities, ensuring visibility into impacts across systems, processes, and other portfolios.
Support the creation of an integrated cross‑portfolio delivery plan by aligning project investments with business and technology strategies.
Partner with divisional leadership to identify resource needs and staff programs and projects with appropriately skilled team members.
Work closely with Technology leaders to define priorities, objectives, scope, and deliverables that support enterprise goals and desired business outcomes.

Delivery Oversight & Governance:

Oversee the successful delivery of complex technology programs and projects within the assigned portfolio, ensuring alignment to business value, timelines, and budget.
Analyze incoming demand and structure it into programs, projects, or epics as appropriate.
Apply appropriate Governance Frameworks to guide business case development and ensure required documentation and approvals are in place.
Lead and develop a team of Program Managers and Project Managers accountable for delivery execution.
Conduct regular program retrospectives and post‑implementation reviews to drive continuous improvement and capture lessons learned.
Manage portfolio‑level risks and issues, ensuring effective analysis, mitigation, communication, and resolution.
Synthesize portfolio performance, financial forecasts, risks, dependencies, and delivery outcomes into clear, concise, and decision-oriented communications for senior leadership and governance forums. Proactively surface emerging concerns, articulate business impacts, and recommend practical courses of action.
Maintain detailed portfolio‑level spend plans and ensure strong financial governance across all initiatives.
Serve as the escalation point for all delivery‑related issues, risks, decisions, and changes within the portfolio.
Manage resource capacity, workload balancing, and team assignments to ensure optimal delivery performance.
Apply the most appropriate delivery methodologies—Waterfall, Agile (Scrum/Kanban), Hybrid, etc.—to achieve optimal business outcomes, ensuring adherence to enterprise standards and methodologies.

What you will bring:

A university or college degree in a relevant field.
A minimum of eight years of progressive technology delivery experience within financial services, insurance, fintech, or a comparably complex organization, including at least three years leading multi-million-dollar programs, portfolios, or enterprise initiatives. Experience with application development and technology modernization is preferred.
Proven ability to build strong, collaborative relationships with colleagues and external stakeholders, influencing outcomes with confidence and credibility.
Proven executive-level communication skills, with the ability to translate complex portfolio, delivery, financial, and risk information into clear, concise, decision-oriented messages for senior leaders. Demonstrated experience preparing and delivering executive presentations, facilitating governance forums, influencing senior stakeholders, and communicating difficult issues or recommendations with confidence, sound judgment, and appropriate transparency.
Demonstrated portfolio management experience, including investment planning, prioritization, financial forecasting, capacity planning, dependency management, and the evaluation of competing initiatives against business value and strategic outcomes.
Proven ability to apply sound judgment and constructive challenge within governance forums, including testing assumptions, identifying gaps, escalating concerns, and helping senior leaders make informed investment and delivery decisions.
Demonstrated experience leading and developing delivery professionals, including setting clear accountabilities, coaching performance, building succession capability, and creating an environment of transparency, inclusion, and continuous improvement.
Ability to work across organizational boundaries and influence business and technology leaders with competing priorities, building alignment around enterprise outcomes rather than optimizing for a single project, function, or portfolio.
A strategic mindset with the ability to evaluate programs through the lens of business value and enterprise outcomes.
Strong comfort with ambiguity and change, with the ability to navigate uncertainty by seeking clarity from diverse stakeholders and available information.
Exceptional multi‑tasking and prioritization skills, thriving in a fast‑paced and demanding environment.
A passion for building, developing, and empowering high‑performing teams; a leader who models continuous learning, innovation, and an entrepreneurial mindset.

About Destination Canada

Tourism is the heartbeat of communities from coast to coast to coast. At Destination Canada, our aspiration for the tourism industry is to generate wealth and wellbeing for all of Canada and enrich the lives of our guests. Our mission is to influence supply and build demand for the benefit of locals, communities and visitors through leading research, alignment with public and private sectors, and marketing Canada nationally and abroad. We seek diverse, ingenious thinkers teeming with intellectual curiosity and a deep desire to grow Canada's tourism industry – strengthening the socio-cultural, environmental and economic vitality tourism brings to Canada.

About the role:

Reporting to the Senior Vice President, Marketing Strategy & Chief Marketing Officer, the Regional Managing Director, Asia Pacific provides strategic direction and leadership for Destination Canada's activities across China, Japan and South Korea. The role translates Destination Canada's 2030 Vision and Go-to-Market Strategy into regional priorities and initiatives that strengthen Canada's brand, build demand among high-value travellers and contribute to organizational objectives.

The Regional Managing Director leads regional teams and operations, develops strategic partnerships across the travel and tourism ecosystem, and connects regional opportunities with global initiatives and travel corridors. Working closely with colleagues in Canada and international markets, the role uses market intelligence, partner insights and performance data to guide decisions, oversee resources and deliver measurable results.

Regional Strategy: Develops and implements regional strategies for China, Japan and South Korea, translating Destination Canada's 2030 Vision and Go-to-Market Strategy into market priorities that contribute to global objectives and high-value travel demand. Strategic Partnerships: Develops long-term partnerships with airlines, travel brands, media, distribution platforms and other organizations, connecting regional opportunities with broader partnership ecosystems to extend reach, share capabilities and deliver measurable impact.
Marketing and Discoverability: Oversees integrated marketing initiatives that strengthen Canada's cultural relevance, build destination demand and improve Canada's discoverability across evolving digital, search and AI-enabled travel planning channels, in collaboration with global teams and partners.
Trade Engagement: Guides regional travel trade and distribution strategies, strengthening industry relationships, advocacy and collaboration to increase awareness of Canadian tourism experiences and support travel conversion.
Market Intelligence: Uses consumer research, travel flow insights, partner data and emerging insights into AI-enabled discovery and traveller behaviour to identify opportunities, inform regional priorities and support investment decisions.

People Leadership: Leads and develops regional employees and external representatives, setting priorities, managing performance and fostering collaboration across markets and with headquarters teams.
Performance Management: Establishes regional performance objectives, monitors results and applies insights from marketing, partnership and operational activities to improve effectiveness, resource allocation and measurable outcomes.
Financial Oversight: Oversees regional operating and program budgets, resource allocation, forecasting and contract management, ensuring effective stewardship of resources and compliance with organizational policies.
External Representation: Represents Destination Canada with government officials, tourism industry leaders, strategic partners and other stakeholders, advancing organizational priorities and strengthening Canada's position within the regional tourism ecosystem.

Graduation from a recognized university in marketing, business, tourism or another relevant discipline, or an acceptable combination of education, training and experience.

Executive communication and stakeholder engagement: Ability to present strategic recommendations clearly, influence decisions and build effective relationships with senior government, industry and business stakeholders across cultures.

About Nomic

Nomic was founded to make biology easier to measure—and to enable scientists to extend lives by making proteomics accessible, scalable, and routine. Our story began at McGill University, where our co-founders and early team developed breakthrough technology that would change the way proteins are measured.

Today, Nomic is powered by our proprietary nELISA® platform—an end-to-end technology that delivers high-throughput, quantitative, and affordable protein data at unprecedented scale. With the launch of Omni 1000, we are making the $50 proteome a reality, breaking down barriers that have limited the field for decades. For the first time, large-scale, quantitative proteomics is accessible to any scientist, supporting everything from drug discovery and translational research to AI-enabled therapeutic development.

Since our launch, we’ve partnered with leaders in pharma, biotech, and academia—including GlaxoSmithKline and the Broad Institute—and have profiled more than 500,000 samples across diverse applications. Our growth is fueled by over $60 million in investment from top-tier backers, including our recent $42 million Series B.

We’re building a team of world-changers—scientists, engineers, and problem-solvers who believe that accessible proteomics can help shape the future of medicine. If you want your work to have real impact, we’d love to meet you.

Learn more in our Series B announcement.

The role

As Director, Supply Chain, you will oversee end-to-end supply chain operations, including procurement, logistics, and inventory management. You will drive the development and execution of strategies to optimize performance, reduce costs, and improve reliability across systems and workflows. This role involves close collaboration with cross-functional teams to align production schedules, streamline material flow, and mitigate supply risks. You will also lead data-driven forecasting, manage supplier relationships, and establish clear metrics to monitor and continuously improve supply chain effectiveness. This role is ideal for someone with a strong track record in a high-growth environment, particularly in life sciences, and experience operating at the intersection of manufacturing and services.

What You’ll Do

Procurement

Own our material and product costs within our standard cost model, analyzing cost structure and inventory variances and leading improvements in cost efficiency.
Design and maintain procurement workflows that are scalable, automated and audit-ready, including for materials used in quality-controlled processes.
Develop sourcing strategies and manage supplier relationships, from negotiation to ongoing performance oversight.
Work with Sales, Manufacturing and Service Lab leaders to forecast material needs, using data-driven models and increasingly automated tools.

Sales and operations planning

Lead materials and supply planning with operational leaders, aligning production plans, raw material supply, inventory and supplier capacity with the sales forecast.
Build and maintain operational and capacity models that support resource planning and budgeting.
Own our ERP as its subject matter expert: data integrity, accuracy and how well it serves the business.

Inventory

Own our inventory systems and processes, with tight integration between the ERP and Nomic’s internally developed LIMS, the central hub for our operational data.
With your peers, set inventory carrying strategies that balance operational performance and financial stewardship.
Oversee receiving: intake, verification and system entry of inbound materials.
Keep physical inventory accurate across all storage sites, including temperature-controlled storage, and own material movement, reconciliation and audit readiness.
Track raw materials, work in progress and finished goods end to end, including lot traceability and shelf life.

Logistics

Build and run outbound logistics for our kit business: order fulfillment, packaging, shipping, temperature-controlled distribution, delivery tracking and returns.

What You’ll Bring

You’re naturally curious, quick to learn and energized by solving problems with people across disciplines. You think end to end, from planning and procurement to inventory and logistics, and you want to design systems that work well and scale from day one. You bring an engineering mindset, you’re comfortable with technology, and you care about making things run smoothly, reliably and transparently. You approach operations practically and iteratively, always looking for the next improvement.

You’ve seen what good looks like in a fast-growing manufacturing organization like ours. You know when to move fast, when to push back and when to step in and fix something yourself. You adapt how you work with others, handle change and ambiguity well, and colleagues trust you to bring structure without rigidity. You’re excited to be one of the first leaders of this function, knowing your work will help scientists better measure and understand biology.

Relevant experience. 7+ years in supply chain, operations or manufacturing roles supporting manufacturing. Life-science tools experience is strongly preferred; we also welcome candidates from other industries with strong technical adaptability.
Leadership and building experience. Experience leading and developing people. Building scalable processes in a high-growth company or having led a supply chain function is a plus.
Procurement and cost expertise. Experience owning strategic sourcing and supplier negotiations, and working with standard costing and variance analysis. Experience developing procurement practices in a quality-controlled environment is a plus.
Planning and inventory experience. Experience connecting sales forecasts to production and materials planning, with ownership of manufacturing inventory control. Experience shipping temperature-controlled goods is a plus.
ERP expertise. Subject matter expertise in an ERP system; NetSuite is highly desirable.
Cross-functional communication. You work effectively with scientific, operational and commercial teams and can turn complex requirements into practical processes.
Education. An advanced degree (for example an MSc) in engineering, the life sciences or a related technical field is a plus.
Location. You can work on-site in Montréal about half the time. Working proficiency in French and English is an asset.

Why join us

Real ownership. You’ll set the direction for Supply Chain and shape the processes, systems and workflows that support Nomic’s growth.
Work that matters. Our platform helps pharma, biotech and academic scientists understand disease and develop new medicines. A reliable supply chain is what keeps it running.

You'll lead the Credit Valuation Adjustment (CVA), Funding Valuation Adjustment (FVA), and Collateral Valuation Adjustment (ColVA) mandates while supporting the continued evolution of the broader XVA framework, including Margin Valuation Adjustment (MVA) and capital-related valuation adjustments, where applicable. new_jobs.title: Managing Director, XVA Management
new_jobs.description:
We’re building a relationship-oriented bank for the modern world. We need talented, passionate professionals who are dedicated to doing what’s right for our clients.

At CIBC, we embrace your strengths and your ambitions, so you are empowered at work. Our team members have what they need to make a meaningful impact and are truly valued for who they are and what they contribute.

To learn more about CIBC, please visit CIBC.com

What You'll Be Doing

As the Managing Director, XVA Management, you'll provide senior front-office leadership for the pricing, transfer, hedging, and portfolio management of valuation adjustments arising from counterparty credit risk, funding, collateral, initial margin, liquidity, and regulatory capital across Global Markets. You'll lead the Credit Valuation Adjustment (CVA), Funding Valuation Adjustment (FVA), and Collateral Valuation Adjustment (ColVA) mandates while supporting the continued evolution of the broader XVA framework, including Margin Valuation Adjustment (MVA) and capital-related valuation adjustments, where applicable. In this role, you'll combine strong trading judgment with strategic leadership to help optimize transaction structuring, improve resource efficiency, and support disciplined risk-taking. You'll oversee desk strategy, financial performance, governance, and infrastructure priorities while building the talent, operating model, and capabilities required to support broader desk-head responsibilities over time.

At CIBC we enable the work environment most optimal for you to thrive in your role. To successfully perform the work, you’ll be on-site full-time.

How You'll Succeed

Lead XVA trading and portfolio management - Lead the pricing, risk transfer, hedging, and portfolio management of CVA, FVA, and related valuation adjustments across Global Markets, with accountability for desk profit and loss (P&L), risk appetite, and limit usage.
Deliver strategic transaction advice - Provide timely XVA pricing and strategic transaction guidance to Sales and Trading, including assessment of counterparty credit, funding, collateral, margin, liquidity, and capital impacts.
Manage risk with discipline - Manage material market, credit spread, jump-to-default, wrong-way, basis, funding, and model risks, and establish effective hedging strategies, particularly during periods of market stress.
Oversee desk performance and controls - Oversee daily P&L and risk, explain key drivers and sensitivities, challenge unusual movements, and ensure timely escalation of valuation, model, data, control, or limit issues.
Drive funding and capital efficiency - Partner with Central Funding, Treasury, and Global Markets Resource Optimization to improve funding, collateral, initial margin, leverage, and regulatory capital efficiency across Global Markets.
Strengthen collateral strategy and operating effectiveness - Provide senior oversight and advisory support to the Collateral Operations Group, including guidance on collateral strategy, complex transactions, disputes, control issues, and enhancements to operating effectiveness.
Advance desk strategy and business performance - Own and advance the desk strategy, annual plan, financial objectives, and management reporting, identifying opportunities to improve risk-adjusted returns, client competitiveness, and portfolio diversification.
Translate market and regulatory developments into action - Monitor market practice, competitor activity, and regulatory developments affecting counterparty risk, derivatives valuation, capital, margin, and funding, and turn these developments into clear business actions.
Maintain strong governance - Maintain effective governance for valuation, reserves, risk transfer, new products, and transaction approvals, and represent the desk at relevant risk, valuation, capital, and business governance forums.
Set the direction for analytics and infrastructure - Set priorities for XVA analytics, models, data, and technology, and sponsor automation, scalable controls, and infrastructure enhancements in partnership with Quantitative Analytics, Technology, and Operations.
Act as a trusted senior advisor - Serve as a senior escalation point for complex or material transactions, communicating recommendations, portfolio risks, and performance clearly to Capital Markets senior management and control functions.
Promote a strong risk and team culture - Promote a strong risk and conduct culture, ensure compliance with all applicable governance, control, regulatory, and policy requirements, and build a high-performing, inclusive team through disciplined hiring, coaching, succession planning, performance management, and development.

Who You Are

You have a degree in finance, mathematics, economics, engineering, or a related discipline. An advanced degree or relevant professional designation is an asset.
You have deep senior markets experience. You bring 12 or more years of relevant markets experience, including significant senior XVA trading responsibility and leadership of people, risk, P&L, or a material portfolio.
You bring deep XVA and derivatives expertise. You have strong knowledge of CVA, FVA, ColVA, MVA, and capital-related valuation adjustments, along with counterparty exposure, netting, collateral and margin mechanics, funding, liquidity, and the accounting and regulatory frameworks relevant to derivatives.
You have broad cross-asset knowledge. You bring expertise across interest rates, foreign exchange, credit, equities, and commodities, along with a strong understanding of market, credit spread, jump-to-default, wrong-way, basis, and model risk.
You turn complexity into clear decisions. You can translate complex risk, valuation, and capital considerations into commercial decisions, transaction structures, and clear recommendations for clients and senior management.
You demonstrate sound judgment under pressure. You have a disciplined approach to risk management, a strong control orientation, and the ability to lead through volatile markets and significant incidents.
You have strong strategic planning, financial management, and stakeholder influence skills. You have the credibility to represent the desk in senior governance forums and with control partners.
You are a caring and accountable leader. You have experience developing and implementing strategic team goals. You have experience coaching employees and inspiring successful team performance.
You're digitally savvy. You seek out innovative solutions and embrace evolving technologies. You can easily adapt to new tools and trends.
You are an effective communicator. You bring strong negotiation, relationship management, and client service skills, along with a commitment to collaboration, inclusion, and professional conduct.
You live your values. You bring high standards, genuine care to your relationships, and want to grow with an employer that shares your values and brings out your best.

What CIBC Offers

At CIBC, your goals are a priority. We start with your strengths and ambitions as an employee and strive to create opportunities to tap into your potential. We aspire to give you a career, rather than just a paycheck.

We work to recognize you in meaningful, personalized ways including a competitive salary, incentive pay, banking benefits, a benefits program*, defined benefit pension plan*, an employee share purchase plan, a vacation offering, wellbeing support, and MomentMakers, our social, points-based recognition program.
Our spaces and technological toolkit will make it simple to bring together great minds to create innovative solutions that make a difference for our clients.

We are looking to bring on a VP into our Global Finance Risk team, to be based out of the Toronto office.

This person will be responsible for managing risk across prime, counterparty credit, and business and developing the risk framework, which includes margin risk methodologies. The person will also collaborate across teams, including trading, credit, market risk, counterparty, and the front office to work cohesively and collaboratively to ensure all risk coverage. They will also be responsible for stress testing and scenario analysis for the business.

The role provides direct risk oversight of a business supporting sophisticated counterparties and structured financing activity. Responsibilities extend beyond routine monitoring and require both technical risk expertise and sound judgment.

The resource would be expected to:

Support the counterparty and platform risk management of BMO’s cash and synthetic Prime Brokerage and Equity Delta One business lines
Solutions-oriented client engagement throughout the lifecycle of a client
First line of defense in risk managing credit risk and monitoring platform exposure
Generation of key risk analytics and development of new tools to support insights and emerging risk trends
Understanding market and credit risks within Prime products and effectively communicating to senior management and control functions
Evolving the risk framework and other risk governance items to ensure a proper control environment and strategic platform development
Support senior team members in responses to Regulatory inquiries and periodic requests
Key in-business coverage for emerging counterparty risk events and crisis management
Contributes to growing / elevating the BMO and BMO Capital Market Prime Brokerage brand with a commitment to and presence in the community
Balances the Bank's risk appetite with the client needs in making recommendations/proposals
Manages firm’s risk and takes action to reduce exposure in developing and delivering client strategies
Take measured risks while protecting the bank by applying our Risk Management Framework in the execution of your role, in line with our Risk Culture and within our approved Risk Appetite, making sound and risk informed decisions that align to business strategy, protect assets, and adhere to applicable policy documents (Frameworks, Policies, Standards, Procedures and Supporting documents), laws and regulations.

Job Background / Context:

Global platform includes Prime Brokerage and Swap offerings across US, Canada and the UK.
Client portfolios comprise of a broad range of asset classes and investment strategies, including: Equities (incl. Common Stock, ETFs, ADRs, MLPs, REITs), Corporates (IG & HY), Convertible Bonds, Options & Indexes
Hedge fund and real money counterparties

Key Responsibilities:

Daily management of client portfolio exposures and counterparty-related risk issues
Support of operational risk and platform trade processing associated with client counterparty risks
Participation in prospective client pitches and term negotiations, modeling commercial risk terms and constructing incentives to support strategic, risk-efficient returns growth through ongoing client dialogue
High level of engagement with Sales, Trading and other members of the business as it relates to client management and ongoing business initiatives
Thoughtful and complete analysis and communication of risk concerns both internally within the business and among control function partners
Identifying and escalating emerging risks – credit, market, operational or legal – to senior management and Global Finance management. Continuously assessing and adapting to new products and market stress events and proactively proposing risk solutions
Facilitating new client trades and managing existing portfolio exposures to ensure that risks, primarily market-driven counterparty risk, but also documentation, legal and reputational risks are well-controlled
Work closely with Counterparty Credit, Credit Risk Management and other key stakeholders on onboarding of new clients, implementation of margin methodology, as well as maintaining ongoing dialogue and promptly escalating issues with existing clients
Develop strategic risk solutions, analytics and platform enhancements to help advance BMO’s competitive advantage
Maintain a positive culture within the team by cultivating a productive and collaborative work environment
Ensure full compliance with risk procedures and other Global Finance or Global Markets policies

Qualifications:

B.S. – Quantitative Finance, Financial Engineering, Finance / Statistics or related discipline.
Between 5 - 7 years of experience in Prime Finance risk or general experience with Delta One and Global Prime Finance trading
Experience with VaR and stress testing.
Strong data querying and quantitative analysis skills are required, knowledge of Python, SQL and AI Development tools.
Comfort with using data querying skill set to design risk dashboards, graphic user interfaces linked to internal databases and enhanced risk reporting.
Exposure to and strong understanding of equities products, such as Delta One, Swaps, and derivatives across all asset classes. Experience with Synthetic Prime is a plus.
Strong understanding of market risk and counterparty risk processes and metrics.
Knowledge of relevant Prime financing platforms, asset types, market structure and client investment strategies.
Experience with data infrastructure transformation, financial engineering and/or quantitative expertise in risk modeling / data analytics.
Experience with risk decision-making authority carrying direct economic impact.
Verbal & written communication skills - In-depth.

Analytical and problem solving skills - In-depth.
